bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic concentration in Maharashtra for both revenue and assets — Maharashtra contributed 69.15%, 71.23%, 68.12% and 58.13% of revenue for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; manufacturing and finishing / warehousing facilities are also concentrated in the state, so a single-state disruption hits revenue and production simultaneously
- Supplier concentration, compounded by the supplier base itself sitting in Maharashtra — Top 10 suppliers contributed 61.07%, 64.49%, 56.93% and 53.02% for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; raw material and stores/consumables sourcing is concentrated in the same state as operations
- Customer concentration without long-term agreements — Top 10 customers contributed 32.43%, 29.24%, 24.15% and 27.52% for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; the Company states it does not have long-term agreements with such customers
- Raw material and consumable price volatility — Yarn and greige fabric are the key inputs for the manufacturing divisions and coal, chemicals and colours for job work; the DRHP flags that increases or fluctuations may adversely impact pricing and supply
- Dependence on corporate and wholesale clients in home textiles and furnishings — 28.17%, 25.18%, 27.87% and 34.47% of manufacturing revenue came from corporate and wholesale clients for H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023; changes in their business models or procurement policies would reduce revenue
- Fast-fashion demand and consumer-preference risk in the home textile / curtain segment — The Company describes its segment as a fast fashion fabric solution vulnerable to variations in demand and changes in consumer preferences
- Historical corporate-compliance defects — The DRHP discloses inadvertent inconsistencies in historical corporate filings, and a past preferential issue where subscription monies were not kept in a separate bank account as prescribed under the Companies Act; a compounding application has been filed and penalties may be imposed
- Reliance on issuer-commissioned secondary industry data — Industry information is drawn from the Ken Research Report commissioned and paid for by the Company exclusively for the Issue, which the DRHP itself flags as subject to inherent risks

business.body: Harit Industries Limited operates as a fully integrated textile manufacturing entity in the Home Textile Sector, managing the entire value chain in-house from design to weaving, processing and finishing. The stated growth path is organic within the existing Maharashtra-based integrated units: the Company was engaged in curtain and upholstery fabrics since incorporation in 2019 and expanded from 2020 into fabric-processing job work for third parties, and it now offers integrated operations across readymade curtains, fabrics for curtains and upholstery, and fabric processing. Manufacturing and finishing / warehousing facilities remain concentrated in Maharashtra.

outlook.body:

- Within the job-work division the customer supplies the fabric, so the cost base is consumables (coal, chemicals, colours) rather than raw material, whereas the manufacturing divisions carry yarn and greige fabric input cost

- Declining contribution from the subsidiary-level yarn and greige fabric trading line, from 12.29% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2024 to 8.00% in Fiscal 2025 and 1.74% in the six months ended September 30, 2025

capacity_notes: The DRHP does not print a unit-of-measure column on the capacity table. The unit is metres: the unit-wise Actual Production figures sum exactly to the auditor-certified "Total Production" KPI stated in metres for every period — 6M ended 30-Sep-2025 = 2,88,63,749; FY25 = 5,98,65,684; FY24 = 5,54,23,270; FY23 = 3,33,89,258.

Installed capacity assumptions stated by the DRHP: (a) uninterrupted operations without lockdowns, strikes or shutdowns; (b) continuous raw material and power supply, scheduled maintenance; (c) no adverse changes in government policies affecting production costs or labour relations; (d) 29 working days per month; (e) 02 shifts of 12 hours each every day.

"Installed Capacity on a Pro Rata Basis represents the Company's actual capacity for the year/period. It reflects adjustments made for any machine additions or deletions during the year, with changes accounted for on a month-by-month basis."

"Installed capacity on a pro rata basis for September has been calculated by capacity per month*6 months" — i.e. the six-month stub installed capacity is a HALF-YEAR base, so the stub utilisation percentages are NOT comparable with the full-year utilisation percentages.
"Capacity utilization has been computed as actual capacity divided by installed capacity (adjusted for number of months of disclosure), multiplied by 100, expressed as a percentage."

Capacity and utilisation information is stated to be based on assumptions and estimates by an independent chartered engineer, including assumptions on number of picks, RPM and thickness of fabric, and has been subjected to rounding off.
This capacity table is not printed in the 'Our Business' extract routed to this domain; it appears in Risk Factor 40 and in the Objects of the Issue chapter of the same DRHP.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Fully integrated (backward and forward) textile manufacturing: the Company manages the entire value chain in-house — from design to weaving, processing and finishing. Two mutually exclusive raw-material routes are used: (i) yarn is procured externally and undergoes the complete in-house process — weaving, dyeing, finishing and conversion into the final product; or (ii) greige fabric is procured directly, bypassing the weaving stage and entering the dyeing process, followed by embroidery / printing and final finishing. Stage 1 is raw material procurement (greige / yarn); Stage 2 is weaving (jacquard/dobby/greige), dyeing, embroidery and print; Stage 3 is packing, cutting and finishing, with cut, roll and readymade warehouses feeding customer dispatch. The embroidery and dyeing process involves two cycles — greige fabric is first sent to the dyeing unit for initial coloration, then to the embroidery unit for machine embroidery, then back to the dyeing unit for final dyeing and finishing, then back to embroidery for quality checks before dispatch to the Kalher warehouse; for jacquard and dobby fabrics the material goes directly from dyeing to the warehouse for dispatch. Weaving is performed on pre-owned Thema Super Excel Loom machines; dyeing uses jigger dyeing, jet dyeing, mercerizing, sanforising, decadising and hot air stenters; embroidery uses computerized multi-head machines with CAD; printing uses digital printers and heat transfer printing machines. In addition to in-house weaving the Company also procures selected greige fabric from third-party suppliers. The DRHP describes the September 2025 acquisition of a fabric processing unit from Aloka Exports (land, building and machinery) for ₹1,951 Lakhs as forming part of the Company's capacity expansion and forward integration strategy. The Company cautions that because it follows a forward-integrated model, reported production figures may reflect overlapping quantities since output from one stage is input to the next, and include internal consumption.

Profit after tax provides information regarding the overall profitability of the business.
EBITDA provides information regarding the operational efficiency of our business as it considers all sources of our core income.
EBITDA Margin is an indicator of the operational profitability and financial performance of Company's business
PAT margin is an indicator of the overall profitability and financial performance of our business.
Debt / Equity Ratio is used to measure the financial leverage of the Company and provides comparison benchmark against peers
Return on Equity is an indicator of our efficiency as it measures our profitability. It shows how efficiently we generate profits from our shareholders.
Return on Capital Employed provides how efficiently the Company generates earnings from the capital employed in the business.

overview.business_model: The Company manages the entire value chain in-house - from design to weaving, processing and finishing - across three core divisions. (1) Fabric for Curtains and Upholstery: production of fabrics for curtains and upholstery through a fully integrated process from design, weaving, dyeing, stitching and finishing at its facilities, sold across economy and premium segments. (2) Fabric Processing (Job Works): fabric processing services on a job-work basis, catering majorly to the apparel segment and the curtain industry, anchored in dyeing services which constitute the major share of fabric processing revenue, plus job-work for weaving and embroidery processing. (3) Readymade Curtain: production of readymade curtains through the same integrated process, sold across economy and premium segments. Additionally, through its Subsidiaries, the Company is engaged in the trading of yarn and greige fabric. Customers include wholesalers, retailers and corporate customers for the readymade curtain and fabric for curtains and upholstery divisions, and textile manufacturers for the fabric processing division. Key raw materials are yarn and greige fabric; for fabric processing the fabric is supplied by customers and key consumables include coal, chemicals and colours. Business is primarily based on purchase orders and job-work assignments with an average lead time for order delivery of 4-6 weeks. In Fiscal 2025 revenue from readymade curtains, fabrics for curtain and upholstery, and fabric processing services was Rs 1,161.52 Lakhs, Rs 4,111.61 Lakhs and Rs 6,377.04 Lakhs respectively, amounting to 9.02%, 31.91% and 49.49% respectively of revenue from operations for the same period.

strategy_growth.detail: The business is significantly influenced by consumer preferences and market trends in the fabrics for curtain and upholstery market. Demand for certain fabric types, designs, colours, textures or finishes may decline over time. Faster design refresh cycles and customised furnishing solutions have changed demand patterns, and the shorter lifecycle of certain curtain and furnishing designs requires continuous innovation. Regional and cultural differences across India's markets require a wide product range across essential, affluent and premium segments, adding complexity to product development, production planning and inventory management. An in-house team of designers is maintained. No material adverse impact from changing trends has been experienced in the past.

strategy_growth.detail: The U.S. administration announced tariffs on products such as automobile, automobile parts, steel and aluminium in the first three months of CY2025 on several major trading partners including India, with a baseline of 10% tariffs on all countries plus an additional individualised reciprocal higher tariff on countries with the largest trade deficits. Introduction of tariffs together with countermeasures is likely to disrupt global trade and increase financial market volatility. The Company states it is not currently engaged in exporting any of its products, but future export activity could be impacted.
strategy_growth.evidence: Baseline tariff of 10% on all countries; additional tariff of 10% on nearly all countries announced April 05, 2025; on April 09, 2025 the U.S. paused differential tariffs for most countries for 90 days excluding China, which would face a higher tariff of 125 percent; "Pursuant to the U.S.-India Bilateral Trade Agreement, the US has reduced the reciprocal tariff on India from 25% to 18%"; U.S. tariffs on imports from India peaked in mid-2025 but were reduced under an early-2026 interim trade understanding.
strategy_growth.title: RF 16 — Changes in international trade policies and increased trade tariffs, including possible U.S. economic or trade sanctions

strategy_growth.detail: The Curtain, Upholstery and Fabric Processing market in India is evolving from a fragmented, largely unorganised setup to a more competitive and structured market. Competition is intensifying around product design, fabric quality, pricing, delivery speed, technological capabilities, brand recognition and regulatory compliance. High quality raw materials, embellishments, design developments and a well-established brand name are the key differentiating factors. The industry is intensely competitive with established domestic and international players in the branded segment, particularly in the curtain space. Failure to compete effectively, including delay in responding to industry and market change, together with increased spending on advertising, may result in a decline in revenues and profitability.

Capital was engineered in the three months before filing. A 13:1 bonus of 1,30,00,000 shares was allotted on 11-Dec-2025 out of 'Capitalisation of Reserves' (Board 26-Aug-2025, AGM 30-Sep-2025), taking issued capital from 10,00,000 to 1,40,00,000 shares; a preferential allotment of 8,32,000 shares at ₹125 (premium ₹115) to 46 allottees followed on 29-Jan-2026, seven weeks before the 19-Mar-2026 DRHP. Two allottees are Promoter Group. Promoters hold 94.39% and Promoters plus Promoter Group 94.57% across 4 of 53 shareholders.

One production line has collapsed while the document claims the opposite. III-B Printing Unit utilisation ran 72.15% (FY23) → 49.50% (FY24) → 21.46% (FY25) → 14.00% (H1FY26 stub, on a half-year capacity base), on installed capacity flat at 292,320 metres; actual production fell 210,908 → 144,684 → 62,744 metres. The claim is defensible for Dyeing III-A, Dyeing IV and Embroidery (95.11-97.58% in FY25) and is not supported for Printing or for Weaving (68.90% FY25).

Group-company financial information is entirely absent. Twelve entities are identified as Group Companies. No revenue, PAT, net worth, reserves, EPS, diluted EPS or NAV is printed for any of them. For the top five (Jai Bhavani Furnishing, Harit Fabtex (India), Daphne Multitrading, Shyamjyot Fabtex, Pratik Panels) the DRHP defers those items to www.haritindustries.com and disclaims that the hosted information forms no part of the offer document; for the remaining seven (Harit Concepts, Sarjai Investment and Finance, Nischay Investment and Finance, Golddust Credit Capitals, Persius Educations, Pandit Ramswaroop Mishra Seva Foundation, Sumo Mercantile) no registered office, website or financials appear anywhere. Six of the twelve are stated to be in common pursuits — the same line of business.

Related-party activity is dense and bi-directional. The AS-18 tables carry 252 lines across 17 named counterparties. In FY25 alone, loan repaid to Harit Concepts ₹1,236.32 Lakhs while loan given to the same entity was ₹276.13 Lakhs, with interest expense ₹66.19 Lakhs and interest income ₹16.00 Lakhs to that one counterparty in the same year; loan repaid to Harit Fabtex (India) ₹964.51 Lakhs; loan given to Daphne Multitrading ₹672.23 Lakhs in H1FY26 against ₹648.58 Lakhs received back. The deleveraging shown in the KPI table had already reversed by the latest balance-sheet date. Debt/Equity rose back to 1.77 at 30-Sep-2025 from 1.47 at 31-Mar-2025: H1FY26 drew ₹2,589.34 Lakhs of long-term borrowings against investing outflow of ₹2,554.71 Lakhs, CWIP went from nil to ₹2,178.36 Lakhs, and capital commitments stood at ₹851.50 Lakhs (₹1,940.00 Lakhs at 31-Mar-2025). Risk Factor 20 states additional borrowings may be incurred after the repayment.

Insurance cover has fallen as the asset base grew. Insured assets covered 39.16% of total insurable assets at 30-Sep-2025, down from 50.07% (FY24-25), 51.16% (FY23-24) and 45.04% (FY22-23), as insurable assets rose ₹9,777.95 → ₹13,522.81 Lakhs while insured assets rose only ₹4,896.14 → ₹5,295.03 Lakhs. Certain policies have recently expired or are nearing expiry and are stated to be under renewal. Machinery is substantially pre-owned imported equipment with a stated residual life of 6-9 years; a fire at subsidiary Sangeeta Texdyes generated a ₹30.24 Lakhs claim in Fiscal 2026.

Statutory-dues discipline has been poor and only recently addressed. Tax deducted at source: 24 instances of delay/non-filing in FY25 with delays of 18-358 days, 35 instances in FY24 (22-85 days), 23 in FY23 (7-87 days) and 7 in H1FY26 (22-83 days). Professional tax 0-95 days in FY25; GST 9 instances in FY23. A Chief Financial Officer (Ms. Vidhi Parekh) was appointed only with effect from 11-Dec-2025, and a Company Secretary and Compliance Officer named as a corrective measure.

Attrition has roughly doubled: 11.11% (FY23) → 22.61% (FY24) → 25.17% (FY25), with 21.37% in H1FY26 stated as not annualised; 55 employees resigned in FY25 against a closing headcount of 223. Contractual labour (307 at 30-Sep-2025) now exceeds direct employees (245).
